subject: [PATCH] mm/compaction: do not skip the free scanner's periodic lock drop

reviews.author: SJ Park
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch's change to count probes instead of pfns may lead to an issue where the scan does not always land on a multiple of COMPACT_CLUSTER_MAX, and requested clarification.

Reviewer suggested leaving certain lines of code unchanged without expressing a strong opinion or blocking the patch

not that bad.  I think that makes sense.  I just wanted to call out this for a

2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's compaction module, which is responsible for compacting free memory pages. The issue arises when scanning compound pages or high-order free pages with a stride above one, causing the lock to be held and interrupts disabled without periodic drops. To fix this, the patch counts probes instead of page frames and checks every COMPACT_CLUSTER_MAX probes for fatal signals, ensuring that the lock is dropped periodically.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan noted that the loop in isolate_freepages_block() works on one page at a time, regardless of its order, and found the patch sensible.

Reviewer noted that the free scanner's periodic lock drop check should count probes instead of pfns to accurately determine when to drop the lock.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense. The loop is working on one page (regardless of its order)
at a time.
